title: Seeing the Unseen: Visual Similarity for Pixel Language Model Adaptation
abstract: arXiv:2608.30541v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Pixel-based language models (LMs) replace traditional tokenizers by processing rendered images of text, making cross-lingual transfer heavily dependent on the visual and structural properties of writing systems. However, the dynamics of adapting these models to low-resource languages with complex morphology and written in unique scripts are not yet explored. Using Tibetan as a case study, we analyze how continued pre-training of pixel-based LMs is influenced by data scale, initial script exposure, and cross-lingual transfer from languages written in other Brahmic scripts. We introduce four rendering-level metrics to quantify visual script similarity. We evaluate downstream performance across three tasks. Our results show that higher orthographic proximity enhances semantic transfer, even under severe data constraints. translated_title: 见所未见：用于像素语言模型适配的视觉相似性
translated_abstract: 基于像素的语言模型（LMs）通过处理文本的渲染图像来取代传统的分词器，这使得跨语言迁移在很大程度上依赖于书写系统的视觉和结构特性。然而，将这些模型适配到具有复杂形态且使用独特文字书写的低资源语言的动态过程尚未被探索。以藏语为案例研究，我们分析了基于像素的语言模型的持续预训练如何受到数据规模、初始文字暴露以及来自其他婆罗米系文字书写语言的跨语言迁移的影响。我们引入了四个渲染层面的指标来量化文字的视觉相似性，并在三项任务上评估下游性能。我们的结果表明，更高的正字法接近度能增强语义迁移，即使在严重的数据限制下也是如此。此外，我们发现基于预训练起点的性能不对称性：虽然多语言预训练……（原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究以藏语为例，提出四个渲染层面的指标来量化文字的视觉相似性，发现更高的正字法接近度能够促进像素语言模型向低资源语言的语义迁移，即使在数据严重受限的情况下也依然有效。
en_tdlr: Using Tibetan as a case study, this paper introduces four rendering-level metrics to quantify visual script similarity and shows that higher orthographic proximity enhances semantic transfer in pixel-based language models, even under severe data constraints.
